Synopsis:
    The article argues that the European airline industry is slowly moving toward US-style consolidation around a few dominant groups (IAG, Lufthansa, Air France-KLM, Ryanair). The Iran war triggered a fuel price spike to ~$1,800/ton, pressuring leveraged carriers, though demand held up and catastrophic collapses were avoided. M&A activity is accelerating (Apollo/easyJet, Lufthansa/ITA, Air France-KLM/SAS/TAP), capacity growth is decelerating, and barriers to new entrants are high. With jet fuel still around $1,500/ton and the Iran situation unresolved, winter 2026 poses further stress for less-hedged carriers. Consolidation is directionally confirmed but will take time.
